subject: Fit results way different when using lavaan 0.6.15 and 0.6.18 for ESEM

messages.author: ea21f7bb0093ce5e
messages.subject: Fit results way different when using lavaan 0.6.15 and 0.6.18 for ESEM
parts:
Hello,
I conducted an ESEM using lavaan 0.6.15 and 0.6-18. The fit results are described below, and I'm trying to understand the underlying reason for the difference:

This is lavaan 0.6.15 -- running exploratory factor analysis
Overview models:
                   chisq  df pvalue   cfi rmsea
  nfactors = 1 45261.791 702      0 0.751 0.068
  nfactors = 2 19332.025 664      0 0.862 0.052
  nfactors = 3 10298.811 627      0 0.920 0.041
  nfactors = 4  6287.099 591      0 0.948 0.034
  nfactors = 5  4704.340 556      0 0.960 0.031

Lavaan 0.6-18 on March 12, 2025 (Personal Laptop)

                   chisq  df pvalue   cfi rmsea
  nfactors = 1 45261.791 702      0 0.915 0.091
  nfactors = 2 19332.025 664      0 0.964 0.060
  nfactors = 3 10298.811 627      0 0.981 0.045
  nfactors = 4  6287.099 591      0 0.989 0.035
  nfactors = 5  4704.340 556      0 0.992 0.031


base_lavaan = read.csv("base_lavaan.csv")
fit <- efa(data = base_lavaan,
           estimator = 'WLSM',
           missing="pairwise",
           ordered = TRUE,
           nfactors = 1:5)
summary(fit)

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Fit results way different when using lavaan 0.6.15 and 0.6.18 for ESEM
parts:
Hello Luis,

I was not sure either. But I ran a single model like this:

fit <- efa(data = base_lavaan,
estimator = 'WLSM',
missing="pairwise",
ordered = TRUE,

nfactors = 1, output = "lavaan")
summary(fit, fit.measures = TRUE)

and the difference has to do with the choice for the regular/old
'scaled' version of the CFI/RMSEA (0.6-15), or the new 'robust' version
(0.6-18 and higher) which was implemented in newer versions of lavaan.

See

Savalei, V. (2021). Improving fit indices in structural equation
modeling with categorical data. Multivariate Behavioral Research, 56(3),
390-407. doi:10.1080/00273171.2020.1717922

Yves.
